Alia: Pinging the runtime crew — I have a small but reliable repro of a host<->GPU page ownership race when offload eviction and async prefetch overlap. Happened on dedicated staging node (p4d-ish), attaching logs inline below.
Marcus: Thanks. Can you drop the repro steps here?
Alia: Steps: 1) Start load with many short chats to keep KV alive. 2) Trigger scheduled async prefetch (prefetch window small). 3) Simultaneously trigger eviction via stress script. Repro command: ```./stress_offload --pages=1200 --prefetch-ms=10 --evict-interval=50``` Logs show sequence: host unmap -> gpu write -> host map (race) -> OOM/panic.
Sasha: Hmm. Sounds like we don't have an atomic ownership handoff. Are you seeing stale GPU pointers used after host map return?
Alia: Yes — stack traces show kernel tries to write to a page that the host thinks it owns. It's timing-dependent; more likely with small prefetch-ms.
Devon: Quick theory: our residency state machine allows "own"->"transfer"->"own" transitions without cross-checking a transfer token. Two concurrent paths can both think they won the transfer.
Marcus: Agreed. We saw similar in old mmap-migration work. We added a syncpoint there. Suggest adding an ownership epoch counter or sequence token with compare-and-swap on handoff.
Sasha: That would be minimally invasive. API sketch: ```bool try_handoff(page_id, from_owner, to_owner, epoch_before) { return CAS(page_meta[page_id].epoch, epoch_before, epoch_before+1) && set_owner(page_id, to_owner); }``` If CAS fails, retry or abort transfer.
Alia: I tried a simpler mutex-per-page but perf hit was visible in microbench. Epoch CAS seems promising. Need to measure tail latency.
Devon: Also want telemetry: increment "handoff_conflict" when CAS fails, and histogram of retries. We can gate-in via feature flag.
Marcus: Action items: - Alia to add failing test (deterministic interleaving) and telemetry stub by EOD (assigned). - Sasha to prototype epoch CAS in allocator API (non-blocking) and bench. - Devon to add feature-flag and dashboard metric names.
runtime-bot: CI pipeline: test/offload/race_check started by Alia — build 7432 queued.
Sasha: One more note on tradeoffs — CAS reduces conflicts but might be futile if transfer requires long IO. We need a backoff strategy: exponential backoff up to X ms then fall back to global slow-path lock.
Marcus: Good point. Document fallback semantics: optimistic fast path (CAS), short spin with backoff, then slow-path lock that also updates audit log for debugging.
Alia: I'll include a tiny reproducer in tests/ that toggles prefetch/evict timing via env vars. Will paste PR when CI finishes. :thumbsup:
Devon: For rollout, let's gate on a metric threshold: if "handoff_conflict" > 0.1% of ops for 5m, abort canary and revert. Also add a debug dump on slow-path to help postmortems.
Marcus: Sounds like a plan. If Sasha's bench shows <2% p99 overhead we can ship to canary next week.
Alia: OK. I'm on it. Will follow up with PR (#) and perf numbers. :eyes:
